headline: Security and sandboxing is the largest confirmed area of the product — process containment, resource caps, network blocking, certificate trust and the configurable security rulebase are all backed by code, while five items including the Hyper-V sandbox, prompt-injection fencing, audit retention and role-based permissions could not be confirmed from what was reviewed.
what_is_there: The code shows untrusted commands being run inside a restricted Windows container with CPU, memory and disk caps, timeouts and network access blocked by default, plus a lower-privilege execution mode and routing of commands to different containment levels by risk. There is also automatic trust handling for self-signed certificates with a certificate-bundle override, a configurable security rulebase that feeds into prompt, attachment and command checks, and action logging of tool calls, permission decisions and blocked actions.
what_is_unclear: The review could not settle five items: the Hyper-V-based sandbox VM (configuration for it exists but no implementing code was seen), prompt-injection detection and fencing, the retention half of the audit log ticket (logging is present, automatic pruning or rotation was not seen), role-based access control for workspaces and tasks, and an in-progress review of the rulebase constraints, which by nature leaves no trace in code. Note also that the ticket for file integrity verification is backed by code that does privilege-level isolation rather than file checksum verification, and the URL-guard and macro-blocking parts of the network ticket were not visible.
suggested_action: Ask the team to confirm three specific points: whether the Hyper-V sandbox is actually built or only configured, whether audit logs are pruned on any schedule, and whether the 'Integrity Sandbox' ticket was meant to cover file integrity checking or privilege isolation. Also confirm whether the TLS certificate trust work, which looks complete in the code, can be moved off 'In Progress'.
